governance.attested_by: ercot79 corrected-outages keeper, session 2026-07-17 (the ERCOT-79 availability-envelope audit). This is the deposed 2026-07-17-ercot76-ne-import keeper recipe (zero ScenarioConfig deltas) re-solved on CORRECTED CAMPD facility-outage data. Owner directive 2026-07-17: 'we can't have a keeper on inaccurate data' — the phantom-outage fix is adopted, this run becomes the ERCOT keeper, and ERCOT reverts to NOT-YET because the keeper recipe does not calibrate on the corrected fleet.
governance.note: ERCOT-79 fixed a confirmed CAMPD facility-outage DETECTOR bug: the run-based detect_outages marks a generation run 'available' only when it sustains CF>5% for >=24 CONSECUTIVE hours, so a daily-cycling combined-cycle unit (runs the afternoon peak, shuts overnight) never qualifies and its whole operating season folds into one phantom hard-availability=0 window (T H Wharton, ORIS 3469: zeroed all summer 2023 while its own CEMS shows it generating 1,105 h at up to 813 MW; ~1.9 GW proven-online capability deleted on the 58h over-shoot set). Fix (source-faithful, measured CAMPD cf + EIA-930 net load only): event-based detection for the daily-cycling classes (CC_REGULAR/CC_CHP/CT_CHP/CT_PEAKER) + a revealed-availability filter that keeps a span only where the unit was actually DOWN during its high-net-load hours. Validated: 58h false-outage 1,904 -> 0 MW/h, 0% genuine-outage over-correction (Petra Nova/Sandy Creek/Victoria/Frontera dead-stops preserved). RESULT: the corrected data resolves the 2023 summer over-shoot ($1,068 -> $242 lw on the 58h set, actual $421 — confirming the ERCOT-78 diagnosis) but UN-CATCHES the real scarcity tail (2023 C3c 179 -> 53h vs RT 181, Aug caught 71 -> 25, 2025 tail 19 -> 0; 46 real-scarcity Aug hours actual RT $1,131 fell model $767 -> $78). This is a genuine structural finding, not an over-correction (a clean fix collapses the tail identically): the ERCOT offer/scarcity calibration (offer curves, ORDC/co-opt) was tuned against a phantom-tightened fleet and rests on that phantom room exhaustion. Per CLAUDE.md rule 11 the accurate input is kept and the compensating miscalibration is exposed, not buried. This keeper is therefore NOT-YET; the open lane is a full ERCOT offer/scarcity re-calibration against the corrected availability envelope. See results/calibration/FINDING-ercot79-phantom-outage-2026-07.md. CROSS-ISO: the detector is shared — PJM's committed facility csv shows a stronger phantom signature (164 windows >1500h, an 8784h full-year window) and all six ISOs' unit-level extracts use the same detector; each is its own regenerate-and-re-audit lane (owner-flagged).

exceptions.magnitude: 53h vs RT actual 181h (0.29x, FAIL — rubric v2.7 RT basis); 2024 16h vs 53 (0.30x FAIL); 2025 0h vs 31 (0.00x FAIL)
exceptions.reason: SCARCITY-TAIL COLLAPSE ON CORRECTED OUTAGE DATA (ERCOT-79). The deposed ercot76 keeper caught the real scarcity tail (2023 179h vs 181, Aug caught 119/181) on PHANTOM fleet tightness: the CAMPD facility-outage detector was hard-zeroing ~1.9-5.7 GW of daily-cycling CC capability that its own CEMS shows generating, artificially exhausting the fleet so the multi-product co-opt priced into its ORDC steps. Correcting the detector (measured CEMS + EIA-930, no residual) restores that capability for ALL hours, so the co-opt now has ample event-time room and no longer prices the real August/summer scarcity (46 real-scarcity Aug hours, actual RT $1,131, fell model $767 -> $78). One availability mechanism owned BOTH the Jun/Sep shoulder over-shoot (now fixed, $1,068 -> $242) and the caught August tail (now un-caught). This is out-of-admissible-representation for the CURRENT offer/scarcity calibration, which was fitted against the phantom-tightened fleet; it is NOT a single-lane mechanism gap. Successor lane: re-calibrate the ERCOT offer curves + ORDC/co-opt against the corrected availability envelope so the real scarcity re-forms on real fleet tightness. Until then ERCOT is NOT-YET.
